subject: Renewal: EU + APAC reserved GPU pools — capacity, SLA, and failover plan
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nexgenretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — adding EU / APAC reserved capacity

Hi Evelyn,

Our renewal is coming up for NexGen Retail (deal DX-8421) and procurement has asked us to get a concrete proposal for adding regional reserved capacity. We're looking at a combination of dedicated reserved GPUs in EU and APAC to reduce tail latency for regional storefronts.

High level asks from our side:
- Reserve capacity in EU and APAC (estimate attached forecast)
- Throughput targets to match peak Black Friday traffic in EU (we'll share exact RPS soon)
- Clear failover plan to US region if a regional pool is degraded
- Data residency notes and any additional compliance controls needed for EU customers

Can we set a 30–40 min sync this week? Procurement timeline is tight — aiming to finalize by end of November.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, NexGen Retail
(attachment: nxg_capacity_forecast_oct2026.csv, csv)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — adding EU / APAC reserved capacity

Hi Sophie — thanks for the outline and the forecast.

We can absolutely support dedicated reserved pools in both regions. To make the proposal concrete for procurement we'll need:
- peak token/sec and p95/p99 latency goals per region (you mentioned Black Friday; a sample 1-hour peak RPS would help)
- desired commit term (12 vs 24 months) and any flexibility for burst credits
- whether keys/audit logs must remain in-county for EU (we have options for customer-managed KMS)

Karthik, can you draft a preliminary config and cost sketch that meets the attached forecast? I'll set up a short executive sync with our account team and legal.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:33:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — adding EU / APAC reserved capacity

Thanks Evelyn — quick clarifications from our infra lead:
- Target reserved addition: EU: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (steady pool), APAC: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs (steady pool).
- Latency targets: EU p50 <= 40ms, EU p95 <= 120ms; APAC p50 <= 60ms, APAC p95 <= 180ms.
- Failover: prefer active regional pools, but if EU/APAC are fully degraded we require automatic fallback to our US pool with a max-added tail latency of 150ms for user-facing traffic.
- Data residency: EU customer payloads must not leave EU for storage, telemetry and logs are negotiable if pseudonymized.

Procurement is targeting a signed amendment by 30 Nov. Attaching a more detailed capacity forecast.

Sophie
(attachment: nxg_capacity_forecast_oct2026.csv, csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nexgenretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed config + draft amendment (v1) for DX-8421

Hi Sophie — based on the forecast and latency targets here is a preliminary proposal:

Proposed reserved pools (steady-state):
- EU pool: 8 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs, configured with local KV cache per-region and 256GB KV capacity per GPU.
- APAC pool: 6 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs, similar config.
- US fallback pool: keep existing reserved capacity; configure automated routing policy (priority: local -> local burst -> US fallback) with health checks and a per-request regional preference header.

Throughput & SLOs:
- We will target p50/p95 goals via colocated pools and prefix/KV caching. For deterministic p95 SLAs we recommend adding 20% burst capacity (autoscale credits) to cover traffic spikes — this is included in the quote below.

Commercial summary (sketch):
- 12 month term amendment: incremental +8 EU GPUs +6 APAC GPUs = incremental commit X units/month (detailed pricing attached).
- Throughput guarantee: baseline throughput SLA (tokens/sec) per region; SLA credit formula tied to p95 and availability.

Attached: redwood_draft_amendment_v1.pdf (contains SLO language and proposed pricing).

Next steps:
1) Legal review of amendment language (privacy/data residency clause highlighted).
2) Confirm commit term (12 vs 24 months).
3) Tech deep-dive this week to validate KV sizing for Black Friday.

Happy to hop on a call — propose Thu 22 Oct 16:00 PT for a 30 min sync.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_draft_amendment_v1.pdf, pdf)

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nexgenretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Alex Chung <alex.chung@nexgenretail.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed config + draft amendment (v1) for DX-8421

Appreciate the quick turn, Karthik. A few items from procurement and infra:
- We need explicit SLA credit language for failover scenarios (how credits are calculated if EU falls back to US for X hours).
- Can you confirm whether logs/telemetry used for debugging will reside in EU and be accessible to our security team without leaving the region? If pseudonymization is an option, outline how telemetry is redacted.
- Can we get a conditional DocuSign flow that only activates after legal sign-off on the data-residency clause?

If you can update the amendment with these two bullets and share a v2, procurement will prioritize the signatures.

Sophie

Sophie — looping in account leadership and legal touchpoints. A few updates from our end: 

- We can add a failover SLA section that defines credit calculations where failover increases p95 beyond agreed thresholds; proposed credit = min(25% monthly credit, proportional to minutes of breach). We will draft language for v2.
- Telemetry: we can keep request/response payloads and full logs in-region (EU) if you select our EU Private option + customer-managed KMS. Operational telemetry (aggregates & anonymized metrics) can be replicated out-of-region for platform reliability. We'll capture the exact telemetry types in the amendment.
- Promo: if NexGen signs the incremental commitment by 30 Nov we can extend a one-time 10% expansion credit on the incremental commit for the first 3 billing cycles.

I'll send redwood_draft_amendment_v2.pdf to the thread after legal redlines. HubSpot deal DX-8421 updated (link below).

Best,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Final: amendment v2 and next steps for DX-8421

Sophie / team — thanks for the back-and-forth and for the clear requirements. Summary & next steps from Redwood's side:

Summary of agreement (pending final legal language):
- Incremental reserved pools: EU +8 GPUs, APAC +6 GPUs (A100-equivalent).
- Term: 12 months incremental commit (option to extend to 24 months at revised pricing).
- SLA: regional p95 availability and latency SLOs with failover credit formula (we've added a section to v2).
- Data residency: offer EU Private + CMK option; operational telemetry replicated only as anonymized aggregates unless customer opts in.
- Commercial: 10% one-time expansion credit if signed by 30 Nov 2026.

Attachments: redwood_draft_amendment_v2.pdf (attached). Please route legal redlines to legal@nxg.com and copy us. If procurement confirms, we'll kick off a staged rollout:
1) Pre-provision EU pool and run synthetic load tests (2 weeks)
2) Cutover for a canary group (2 days)
3) Full traffic rollout + Black Friday readiness runbook (1 week)

Sophie — can your procurement confirm the sign-off steps so we can arrange a DocuSign flow that holds the data-residency clause for legal approval? If we get a green light this week, our Delivery team can prioritize EU pre-provisioning for week of 6 Dec.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_draft_amendment_v2.pdf, pdf)
